sections.heading: How Much Power Can a Montclair Roof Produce?

runs.v: When sunlight hits the photovoltaic cells, they produce direct current, and the inverter converts it to the alternating current a home uses, harnessing the sun's energy as a renewable energy source that lowers a household's carbon footprint and energy costs for decades. Output depends on system size, orientation, pitch, and shade; published local estimates put Montclair near 210 sunny days a year. Fixed rooftop panels have no moving parts, so they require minimal repairs, though occasional cleaning helps maintain efficiency, extreme weather can necessitate repairs, and solar installers commonly recommend an inspection every 3 to 5 years. Solar panels typically last 25 to 30 years, and most should run at least 25 years without replacement.

sections.heading: What Incentives Apply to Solar in New Jersey in 2026?

c.v: Is there still a federal solar tax credit? Not for a system a homeowner buys.

runs.v: The IRS states that the Residential Clean Energy Credit equaled 30% of the cost of qualified property installed from 2022 through December 31, 2025, and is not allowed for expenditures made after that date, so federal tax credits no longer cut a 2026 home installation. NJ solar incentives still apply: the NJ Board of Public Utilities' Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) program creates SREC-IIs that earn income for the electricity a system produces; net metering policies let homeowners receive credits from the utility company for excess electricity sent to the grid; New Jersey exempts residential solar installations from state sales tax with Form ST-4; and a certified system can qualify for a property-tax exemption on Form CRES, so solar can increase property value without extra taxes. Solar can help homeowners save money: published estimates put Montclair savings near $1,500 a year and about $51,787 over 25 years, and panels can reduce electric bills by roughly 60 to 80%, though long-term savings depend on the system and the incentives assumed. Rules for solar systems change, so NJ residents should confirm current programs with New Jersey's Clean Energy Program at njcleanenergy.com and a tax professional before they start saving.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of Installing Solar Panels on a Roof?

runs.v: Every mount is a roof penetration, so poor flashing causes leaks; an aging roof has to be replaced first; roof replacements under an existing array mean paying to remove and reinstall the panels; tree cover cuts output; and a homeowner-owned system now carries its full upfront cost. Robust warranties should cover both solar system performance and roofing integrity, so ask who warrants the panels, the mounts, and the roof beneath them.
What Is the 33% Rule for Solar Panels?

Under IRC R324.6, an array covering 33% or less of the roof area needs an 18-inch clear setback on both sides of the ridge, and one covering more needs 36 inches, along with 36-inch firefighter access pathways.
